# PLAN — iteration 2
## Current state assessment
Iteration 1 preserved the required child instance and passed simulation, tool, metric, latency, and timing checks, but routed LUT use stayed at 57, so it failed the strict LUT objective against the timing-feasible incumbent. The next candidate must retain `// @latency 9` and improve routed LUT count while keeping setup WNS and hold WHS nonnegative.

## Hypothesis
Feeding the child an input-valid signal qualified by its existing ready output may let Vivado share the idle-state decode and reduce LUT use without changing accepted transfers.

## Instruction for generator
Keep the unconditional `iterative_divider_core` instance and all top-level ports; add a wire for `in_valid && in_ready` and connect it to the child’s `in_valid` port. Keep the child’s `in_ready`, `quotient`, `remainder`, and `out_valid` outputs directly driving the corresponding top outputs. Preserve reset and cycle behavior; this is only a LUT-area candidate, so retain it only if routed LUT use is strictly below 57 and all verification, metric, setup, and hold gates pass.
